newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Yen depreciation cuts Philippine foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Yen depreciation cuts Philippine foreign debt.

text.p: The steady depreciation of the Japanese yen against the U.S. dollar had reduced the Philippine foreign debt by $570 million, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday.
The yen/dollar rate had slid to 121.4 in late Tokyo trade on Monday from 114.9 at the end of last year.

"The weakening of the Japanese currency to that level will reduce the 1997 yen debt service by $68 million, considering that repayment of yen obligations is spread out over as long as 30 years," the Central Bank said in a statement.
The yen decline has cut the U.S. dollar equivalent of yen-denominated loans approved last year to $1.876 billion from $2.905 billion at the time they were contracted.
The Central Bank estimated that the dollar value of the yen obligations would drop by $1.2 billion for every 10 percent deprecition of the yen against the U.S. dollar.
